data.title: Solving for Unknown Angles
data.description: Practice using angle relationships such as supplementary, complementary, and vertical angles to determine missing measurements in various geometric figures.

challenges.narration: A tile pattern has two lines crossing.
challenges.instruction: x and the labeled angle are vertical angles. Find x.
challenges.hint: Vertical angles (opposite each other where two lines cross) are equal, so x equals the known angle.

challenges.narration: A signpost has two angles that form a right angle.
challenges.instruction: These two angles are complementary (they add to 90°). Find the unknown angle x.
challenges.hint: Complementary angles add to 90°, so x = 90° − the known angle.

challenges.narration: A tile pattern has two angles that sit on a straight line.
challenges.instruction: These two angles are supplementary (they add to 180°). Find the unknown angle x.
challenges.hint: Angles on a straight line add to 180°, so x = 180° − the known angle.

challenges.narration: A garden trellis has three angles meeting at a point.
challenges.instruction: The three angles go all the way around the point (360°). Find the unknown angle x.
challenges.hint: Angles around a point add to 360°, so x = 360° − the two known angles.
